description: Generate Wikipedia-style See Also sections — austere lists of kin objects, concepts, texts, practices, or phenomena adjacent to a given subject without arguing or explaining the kinship. The reader performs the binding. Default deployment is reflexive: produce the See Also for *this conversation* — what would appear at the bottom of the Wikipedia article our chat would constitute. Form rules: bullet list, 5-15 entries, no editorial gloss (brief disambiguating parenthetical only when truly needed), no thesis, mix of obvious and slightly-oblique entries. The slightly-strange entry is load-bearing — where the form's philosophical interest lives. Use when asked 'what's the See Also for this,' 'give me the kin-list,' 'what's adjacent to this,' 'what would appear at the bottom of this Wikipedia article,' 'see also,' 'cf.,' or when a conversation has produced something whose unspoken kinships want to be made visible without being explained. Pairs with /placement, /two-grammars, /bookfy.
